Plot the difference between two htna networks

Source: R/plot_htna_diff.R
plot_htna_diff.Rd

plot_htna_diff() plots the difference between two htna networks: for every transition, how much more (or less) likely it is in one network than in another, for example in the late sessions compared with the early ones. Drawn in the layout of the two heterogeneous networks, the difference network shows whether the change lies within an actor type or in the hand-overs between actors. When the difference comes from a permutation test or a Bayesian comparison, only the differences that the test supports are emphasized.

plot_htna_diff() accepts two htna networks and draws x - y, with positive differences in pos_color and negative differences in neg_color; networks whose node sets differ are aligned on the union of their nodes. It also accepts the result of permutation_htna() or bayes_compare_htna() for two networks, which adds the significance overlay (significant edges solid, the others dashed or hidden with show_nonsig), and the grouped results of either test, drawn as one plot per cohort pair titled with the pair name. It is called for the plot and returns, invisibly, the value of the drawing call, or x for a grouped test result.

For a table of the differences by actor pair use compare_htna().

Usage

plot_htna_diff(
  x,
  y = NULL,
  pos_color = "#009900",
  neg_color = "#C62828",
  group_colors = htna_palette,
  ...
)

Arguments

x

An htna network, or a result of permutation_htna() or bayes_compare_htna() (for two networks or for a grouped network).

y

A second htna network, when x is an htna network. Default NULL.

pos_color

Colour of positive differences. Default "#009900".

neg_color

Colour of negative differences. Default "#C62828".

group_colors

Colours of the actor types, in actor order. Default htna_palette.

...

Further drawing arguments of cograph::splot(), such as title, minimum or, for a test result, show_nonsig.

Value

Called for the plot. Invisibly, the value of the drawing call, or x for a grouped test result.

Conditions

htna_bad_input when x and y are not two htna networks with the same actor types, or a test result was not computed on htna networks; htna_empty_input for an empty grouped result.

See also

compare_htna(), permutation_htna(), bayes_compare_htna(), plot_htna()

Examples

data(human_ai)
early <- build_htna(subset(human_ai, phase == "Early"),
                    actor_type = "actor_type")
#> Metadata aggregated per session: ties resolved by first occurrence in 'session_date' (1 sessions), 'cluster' (18 sessions), 'actor_type' (15 sessions)
late  <- build_htna(subset(human_ai, phase == "Late"),
                    actor_type = "actor_type")
#> Metadata aggregated per session: ties resolved by first occurrence in 'cluster' (24 sessions), 'actor_type' (9 sessions)
plot_htna_diff(late, early)


# a permutation test on the grouped network: one plot per pair of phases
grp  <- build_htna(human_ai, actor_type = "actor_type", group = "phase")
#> Metadata aggregated per session: ties resolved by first occurrence in 'cluster' (24 sessions), 'actor_type' (9 sessions)
#> Metadata aggregated per session: ties resolved by first occurrence in 'session_date' (1 sessions), 'cluster' (18 sessions), 'actor_type' (15 sessions)
perm <- permutation_htna(grp, iter = 50, seed = 1)
plot_htna_diff(perm)
